candidate_sentence_map.S1: AB Pieno Žvaigždės delivered a substantially stronger financial performance in the first quarter of 2026, despite broadly stable revenue.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Sales amounted to EUR 52.064 million, compared with EUR 52.324 million in the first quarter of 2025, a decline of approximately 0.5%.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Sales in Lithuania decreased to EUR 31.405 million from EUR 32.112 million, while sales to other EU countries increased to EUR 11.341 million from EUR 10.801 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: By product category, fresh milk products remained the largest contributor at EUR 42.497 million, while dry milk product sales declined to EUR 1.397 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Cheese and other product sales increased.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Cost of sales fell to EUR 38.078 million from EUR 42.530 million, resulting in gross profit of EUR 13.986 million, up from EUR 9.794 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Other operating income also rose to EUR 363 thousand from EUR 28 thousand.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: These improvements more than offset higher sales and administrative expenses, which increased to EUR 10.983 million from EUR 9.287 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Operating profit before finance costs rose to EUR 3.366 million from EUR 535 thousand.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Net finance expenses were broadly stable at EUR 298 thousand, compared with EUR 308 thousand a year earlier.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: As a result, profit before tax and net profit both increased to EUR 3.068 million from EUR 227 thousand.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Earnings per share rose to EUR 0.07 from EUR 0.01.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: EBITDA increased to EUR 4.730 million from EUR 2.001 million, confirming the substantial improvement in operating performance.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Net cash flow from operating activities was EUR 1.625 million, compared with an outflow of EUR 183 thousand in the first quarter of 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Operating cash flow benefited from higher profitability and a EUR 998 thousand reduction in inventories, although this was partly offset by a EUR 2.536 million increase in receivables.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Investing activities used EUR 551 thousand, mainly for property, plant and equipment, compared with EUR 1.058 million in the prior-year period.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Financing activities resulted in a net outflow of EUR 723 thousand, primarily reflecting repayment of borrowings and finance lease liabilities, whereas the previous year included EUR 8.5 million of loan proceeds.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: Total assets increased to EUR 85.305 million at 31 March 2026 from EUR 83.475 million at year-end.
candidate_sentence_map.S22: Equity rose to EUR 41.164 million, supported by first-quarter profit, while total liabilities declined to EUR 44.141 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S23: Cash increased during the quarter to EUR 2.157 million, although it remained below the EUR 4.902 million reported at 31 March 2025.
candidate_sentence_map.S24: Overall, the period was characterized by stable sales, sharply improved margins and profitability, stronger operating cash generation, and a modest strengthening of the company’s equity position.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: K1-K5, K8-K9 are PRESENT with supporting sentences identified. K6 (cash flows from operating activities) and K7 (current ratio) are MISSING - no mention of operating cash flow amounts or current ratio values. The summary captures most HIGH importance metrics and all MEDIUM importance metrics except two, resulting in a Generally yes rating (score 3). The main picture of improved performance is captured despite these omissions.
